For an H×W grid, make a 3H×2W output. Row ordering is vertically flipped source rows, then original source rows, then vertically flipped source rows. ## Rule inferred from task-1377fd69 (verified correct)

The input is a large regularly tiled grid: thick/background wall lines form rectangular rooms, and most room interiors share a single background color. Some wall-line intersections are recolored. Decode to a smaller room grid:

1. Locate the repeating horizontal and vertical wall lines (the line rows/columns are usually easy to spot because nearly all cells on them share a wall color). Determine the complete rectangles/rooms bounded by consecutive wall lines. 3. Initialize each output cell to the common room-interior color.
4. For each room, inspect the four intersections of its two bounding horizontal lines with its two bounding vertical lines. If all four corners have the same non-wall/special color, use that color for the corresponding output cell. Otherwise leave the room-interior color.
